claims.statement: UseFramework.__call__ is the single execution entry point and performs, in fixed order: a lazy build_root_bus() when was_initialized is false, a SincproFrameworkNotBuilt guard when self.bus is still None, an implicit context overlay push/pop, then delegation to the middleware pipeline with an executor closure that calls self.bus.execute(processed_dto).

build_root_bus() sets was_initialized = True before assigning self.bus from the container, so a first build that fails while materialising the FrameworkBus leaves the instance initialized with bus None; every later framework(dto) call then raises SincproFrameworkNotBuilt, which is recorded with kind="framework".

Lazy root-bus construction is shared by the other entry points, not unique to __call__: with_trace(), with_parent_trace(), get_async_bus() and the entrypoint Catalog all call build_root_bus() when was_initialized is false.

__call__ pushes an implicit isolated overlay initialised from a copy of the shared context only when no overlay is already active on the current task/thread and no global-scope block is in effect, and always pops it in a finally block, including when the call fails.

MiddlewarePipeline.execute stores the original DTO class, runs each middleware in registration order feeding each one the previous return value, and monkey-patches processed_dto.__class__ back to the original when a middleware returned a different DTO type, which is what keeps registry lookup by dto.__class__.__name__ working for transformed DTOs.

An exception raised by a middleware propagates straight out of UseFramework.__call__ to the caller and no error handler (feature, app-service or global) is consulted, because the middleware pipeline runs outside the buses' try/except blocks.

FrameworkBus.execute is pure routing that never executes a handler: it derives dto_name from dto.__class__.__name__, raises DTOAlreadyRegistered if the name is in both registries, dispatches to feature_bus.execute when the name is in feature_registry, else to app_service_bus.execute when the name is in app_service_registry, else raises UnknownDTOToExecute.

The registry keys are the input DTO class __name__ at both registration and lookup time, so two distinct DTO classes sharing a __name__ collide and the decorators raise DTOAlreadyRegistered within a layer; because a name cannot legally live in both registries, the order in which the facade tests feature_registry versus app_service_registry has no observable effect even though the execute docstring describes the opposite order from the implementation.

The cross-layer name collision is checked twice: once in the FrameworkBus constructor at build time and again on every execute call, so the disjointness invariant is re-asserted immediately before routing.

FeatureBus.execute and ApplicationServiceBus.execute share one five-step shape — derive dto_name, open one span with a layer string ("feature" versus "application_service"), emit gated pre-execution logging, dict-lookup the registry and call the handler's execute, then log the truthy response and return it unconverted and untyped — differing only in registry attribute, span layer string and error-reporting layer.

A DTO execution is spanned exactly once, by the sub-bus that runs it: FrameworkBus opens no span of its own and reaches observability only to report framework-level errors, while the FeatureBus span degrades to a nullcontext when OpenTelemetry is unavailable without affecting the call.

Per-bus error handling runs before the facade's: each sub-bus catches the handler exception, reports it on its span with its own layer, and either returns the bus-level handle_error result or re-raises; the facade's handle_error therefore only sees exceptions the sub-bus re-raised or raised itself, and with no handler at either level the facade logs with logger.exception and re-raises the original exception object.

handle_error is one composed callable per bus: build_error_handler_chain folds the registered handlers in reverse so first-registered runs first, and compose_handler delegates to the next handler automatically when a handler re-raises, with the last handler re-raising to the caller; UseFramework keeps three independent chains pushed onto the facade, feature and app-service buses, and handlers registered after build_root_bus() are assigned directly onto the live buses.

return_type is accepted by UseFramework.__call__, the Bus ABC, all three concrete buses and the async/thread wrappers but is never read by any bus body: __call__ forwards it only as kwargs through the middleware pipeline to an executor closure that takes **exec_kwargs and ignores them, so the value returned is always whatever the registered handler's execute returned.

The abstract Bus.execute docstring's promise that a provided return_type yields an instance of return_type (otherwise None) is not implemented behaviour; return_type is a static-typing device expressed in the .pyi overloads, and passing an unrelated class changes nothing at runtime.

The feature_bus injected into every ApplicationService is the same FeatureBus object the facade holds (the container builds app services with framework_container.feature_bus), so a delegated call from an ApplicationService re-enters FeatureBus.execute and opens its own "feature" span within the app-service span.

Framework-level failures are reported but not spanned: only UnknownDTOToExecute and DTOAlreadyRegistered are sent to observability from the facade, with kind="framework", which switches the reported release to the framework's own distribution, and no span is passed so nothing is recorded on a span.

Calling a sub-bus directly with an unregistered DTO raises the bare KeyError from the registry dict lookup inside the sub-bus, not UnknownDTOToExecute — only the FrameworkBus facade raises UnknownDTOToExecute — and that KeyError is still visible to the sub-bus error handler.

build_root_bus() is a lifecycle point that pushes dynamic dependencies onto already-registered handlers, attaches the three error handlers, materialises self.bus, binds every registered handler instance to the framework so self.context resolves to the live overlay, copies the log flags, publishes the DTO-name to DTO-class registry used by introspection, and starts observability; FeatureBus and ApplicationServiceBus are container singletons while FrameworkBus is a factory, so a second build yields a new facade over the same sub-buses and registries.

UseFramework instances are isolated from one another at runtime: each owns its container, registries, overlay ContextVars and Observability object, so two instances in one process never share a bus or report under each other's identity.

sincpro_framework.bus is internal: the public surface is what sincpro_framework/__init__.py exports (UseFramework, Feature, ApplicationService, DataTransferObject, Middleware, logger, TypeDTO, TypeDTOResponse), while the concrete buses are reachable through framework.bus or by importing sincpro_framework.bus directly, which bypasses the middleware pipeline, the implicit overlay and UnknownDTOToExecute.

UseFramework.__call__ is the only caller of MiddlewarePipeline.execute; the two thread/async handles reachable from the same framework (framework.bus.thread_context() and framework.get_async_bus() returning AsyncBus) call Bus.execute directly, so a DTO handed to one of them skips both the middleware chain and the implicit-overlay push.

Every host entrypoint converges on UseFramework.__call__: scalar_executor binds each DTO to a Scalar-callable that calls framework_instance(dto_type.model_validate(payload)), the catalog projection stores that closure as each entry's run, and the MCP and JSON-RPC hosts invoke it, so a wire payload always traverses the same execution path.

All three bus-level failure handlers — FeatureBus.execute, ApplicationServiceBus.execute and FrameworkBus.execute — use a bare except Exception, so a raise derived from BaseException rather than Exception (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit, asyncio.CancelledError) bypasses both observability reporting and every error handler and simply propagates.

A handled failure is indistinguishable from a successful execution at the call site: the sub-bus and the facade both return the handle_error result as the bus response, so the handler is free to return a non-DTO — a handled error can yield a plain string instead of a response DTO.

UseFramework.__call__ has no except clause: nothing above FrameworkBus.execute catches anything, so an exception the facade re-raises (or raises itself, such as DTOAlreadyRegistered or UnknownDTOToExecute with no global handler registered) reaches the caller unchanged, and only the implicit-overlay pop in the finally block still runs.

Middleware failures are not routed through error handling: a middleware that raises a validation error surfaces that middleware's own exception type directly out of UseFramework.__call__, with no feature, app-service or global handler consulted.

Framework-kind errors bypass the Sentry ignore list: because record_error applies the ignored_exceptions filter only when kind == "instance", an UnknownDTOToExecute raised for an unregistered DTO is still reported even when ignore_sentry_exceptions covers Exception, and it is tagged with sincpro.kind == "framework".

Only UseFramework.__call__ turns the post-build bus-is-None state into a reported, catchable framework error: get_async_bus() reaches the same state but guards it with a bare 'assert self.bus is not None', so it fails with a plain AssertionError rather than SincproFrameworkNotBuilt.

The three exception types raised on this execution path (SincproFrameworkNotBuilt, UnknownDTOToExecute, DTOAlreadyRegistered in sincpro_framework/exceptions.py) are not part of the public package surface: sincpro_framework/__init__.py does not re-export them, so callers that want to catch a build or routing failure import from sincpro_framework.exceptions.

The FrameworkBus construction-time collision check is what tests/bus/test_framework_bus.py pins for the same-name-in-both-registries case: registering one DTO name in both sub-buses then constructing FrameworkBus raises DTOAlreadyRegistered before any execution, so that test does not exercise the per-call re-check in FrameworkBus.execute.
